experiment: Six-dimensional sampler compilation with four-layer, 512-unit MLPs
notes: Shared host; the two domains ran on separate A30 GPUs. Compare each compiled run with its own eager baseline.
All models use seed 42 and parameters perturbed away from uniform initialization; eager/compiled copies start identically.
Common arguments plus argument_overrides reproduce a run using benchmarks/torch_compile.py.
Times are seconds. CUDA synchronization surrounds timed blocks. Inference warm confirmations use 100 warmups and 3 repeats of 100 calls; cycle confirmations use 100 warmups and 3 repeats of 30 calls.
Fresh Inductor-cache sampling/cycle rows use separate empty domain/cache-group directories; other system/Triton caches were not purged.
Warm confirmation runs reuse the corresponding domain and cache group. Bulk and CPU use 3 repeats of 10 calls.
Training uses a cheap positive synthetic target and eager Adam; native evaluator, mappings, public adapter, scheduler and IPC are excluded.
Peak allocated/reserved CUDA bytes cover the whole process including base/model copies and are recorded before gradient/snapshot checks. Reserved bytes include allocator history.
42 runs passed. Mixed MLP-only cycle compilation failed at the default eight-variant limit; its limit32 retry passed.
Continuous-only float32 cycles failed the strict gradient tolerance, reproduced in a diagnostic run. No validated speedup is reported for those two failures.
Module/RNG restore checks are same-process, same-execution-mode checks, not fresh-worker or interrupted-window/optimizer recovery.
CPU compiler execution required an installed openssl executable on PATH.
